instruction.name: ldl.d
instruction.description: load left part of an unaligned 64-bit value and merge it into rd

operands.name: rd
operands.description: value merged with the unaligned part

experiments.name: rd merge chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 2000 --unroll2 8000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; st.d $r0, $r20, 8; st.d $r0, $r20, 16; st.d $r0, $r20, 24; li.d $r12, 0' --asm 'ldl.d $r12, $r20, 0'

latencies.notes: MIPS-style unaligned load: rd is read-write, and with a zeroed buffer the merge keeps rd at zero, so a plain chain measures the load plus merge in 4 cycles. The rj and imm paths could not be isolated: any address chase would change rd through the merge.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 2000 --unroll2 8000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; st.d $r0, $r20, 8; st.d $r0, $r20, 16; st.d $r0, $r20, 24; li.d $r12, 0' --asm 'ldl.d $r4, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r5, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r6, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r7, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r8, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r9, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r10, $r20, 0; ldl.d $r11, $r20, 0'
throughput.notes: Read-modify-write load, so it retires two operations per cycle less often than a plain load: 1 CPI against 0.5 for `ld.d`.

notes: LBT MIPS-style unaligned access, measured with a 64-byte-aligned zeroed stack buffer.
